title: Pullback of a compatible line scalar square through all signed powers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites with finite limits and final objects, small relative to a common sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve finite limits and coverings, and write $f^{-1}:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ for its geometric inverse image. Let $R\xrightarrow{\iota}S$ on $\mathcal C$ and $R'\xrightarrow{\iota'}S'$ on $\mathcal D$ be commutative ring sheaves, with maps $a:f^{-1}R\to R'$, $b:f^{-1}S\to S'$ satisfying $b f^{-1}(\iota)=\iota'a$. These define morphisms of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Put $F_R(M)=f^{-1}M\otimes_{f^{-1}R}R'$ and $F_S(N)=f^{-1}N\otimes_{f^{-1}S}S'$, using module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $P,Q$ be locally free rank-one module sheaves over $R,S$, and $P',Q'$ locally free rank-one over $R',S'$ (locally isomorphic to their ring sheaves on coverings of the final objects). Suppose given isomorphisms
$$c:P\otimes_R S\xrightarrow{\sim}Q,\quad c':P'\otimes_{R'}S'\xrightarrow{\sim}Q',\quad p:F_R(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}P',\quad q:F_S(Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q'$$
satisfying $q\circ F_S(c)=c'\circ(p\otimes1)$ under the canonical tensor reassociation $F_S(P\otimes_R S)\cong F_R(P)\otimes_{R'}S'$. Define signed powers $P^{[0]}=R$, $P^{[n]}=P^{\otimes n}$, $P^{[-n]}=\mathcal Hom_R(P^{[n]},R)$ for $n>0$, and similarly for the other three lines, with sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Let $c_m,c'_m$ be the signed scalar comparisons normalized by the unit, positive tensor recursion and the evaluation formula of [lem-pur-signed-line-scalar-tensor-tower]. There exist unique families of isomorphisms $p_m:F_R(P^{[m]})\xrightarrow{\sim}(P')^{[m]}$, $q_m:F_S(Q^{[m]})\xrightarrow{\sim}(Q')^{[m]}$ whose degree-one maps are $p,q$, degree-zero maps are the coefficient-unit maps, positive maps obey tensor recursion, and negative maps are the transpose of pulled-back evaluation followed by precomposition with the inverse positive map. In particular
$$\operatorname{ev}(p_{-n}(z),p_n(w))=F_R(\operatorname{ev})(z\otimes w)$$
under the canonical tensor and unit comparisons, and likewise for $q$. For every integer $m$ one has the equality
$$q_m\circ F_S(c_m)=c'_m\circ(p_m\otimes1)$$
under $F_S(P^{[m]}\otimes_R S)\cong F_R(P^{[m]})\otimes_{R'}S'$. No flatness or invertibility is assumed for $a,b,\iota,\iota'$.

proof.text: Write $A=f^{-1}R$, $B=f^{-1}S$, and $\alpha=f^{-1}\iota$. The supplied inverse image is geometric; its tensor structure is given by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] to the ringed-topos maps defined by $a$ and $b$. This supplies natural tensor isomorphisms $F_R(M\otimes_R N)\cong F_R(M)\otimes_{R'}F_R(N)$, and similarly for $F_S$. The unit map is explicitly $F_R(R)=A\otimes_A R'\to R'$, $x\otimes t\mapsto a(x)t$, with inverse $t\mapsto1\otimes t$; likewise for $S$. These maps and tensor maps use the sheafified sectionwise tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Their normalization on pure tensors determines them, so their unit and reassociation identities are the equality of the corresponding products of scalar factors, by the balancing relations.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; section-tensor-product, balanced tensor and unit formulas

proof.text:
For any $R$-module sheaf $M$, apply the tensor comparison also to the inverse image with target ring $A$. It identifies $f^{-1}(M\otimes_R S)$ with $f^{-1}M\otimes_A B$. The required reassociation is therefore
$$\Theta_M:(f^{-1}M\otimes_A B)\otimes_B S'\longrightarrow(f^{-1}M\otimes_A R')\otimes_{R'}S',\qquad (x\otimes y)\otimes t\longmapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes b(y)t.$$
Its inverse sends $(x\otimes r')\otimes t$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes\iota'(r')t$. The relation $b\alpha=\iota'a$ makes both formulas balanced over $A$; balancing over $B$ and $R'$ shows that both composites are the identity. The formulas induce sheaf morphisms by the sheafification in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. They are natural in $M$, since replacing $x$ by any module morphism's value commutes with both formulas.

source.place: Tag 03EL and section-tensor-product, scalar associativity formulas specialized to the commutative coefficient square

proof.text: Set $p_0$ equal to the unit map and $p_1=p$. For $n\geq1$ define $p_{n+1}$ as the tensor comparison for $F_R(P^{[n]}\otimes_R P)$ followed by $p_n\otimes p$. Each map is an isomorphism, by induction. Define $q_n$ in precisely the same way with $F_S$ and $q$. This is the required positive recursion of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. On a covering where $P$ has basis $e$, $P^{[n]}$ has basis $e^{\otimes n}$: the explicit maps $R\otimes_R R\rightleftarrows R$, $r\otimes s\mapsto rs$ and $r\mapsto r\otimes1$, give the assertion inductively. Thus each $P^{[n]}$ is finite locally free; the same argument applies to $Q,P',Q'$.

source.place: Tag 03EL; section-tensor-product, recursive tensor powers and the rank-one multiplication chart

proof.text:
For $n>0$ apply [lem-pur-ringed-site-finite-free-dual-pullback] to $L=P^{[n]}$ and the ring map $a$. The common size convention, finite limits, covering preservation and finite local freeness required there are exactly our hypotheses and step 3. Its evaluation-defined isomorphism is
$$\delta_R:F_R(P^{[-n]})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom_{R'}(F_R(P^{[n]}),R').$$
Define $p_{-n}(z)=\delta_R(z)\circ p_n^{-1}$. Precomposition with an isomorphism is invertible, with inverse precomposition with $p_n$, directly from [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Thus $p_{-n}$ is an isomorphism and
$$\operatorname{ev}(p_{-n}(z),p_n(w))=\delta_R(z)(w)=F_R(\operatorname{ev})(z\otimes w),$$
with the tensor and unit maps of step 1 understood. The same construction for $Q^{[n]}$, $b$, and $q_n$ gives $q_{-n}$ and its evaluation identity. No general internal-Hom base-change theorem or flatness is used: the cited dual theorem expressly covers finite locally free sheaves and arbitrary coefficient maps.

source.place: Tag 0GMX, remark-pullback-internal-hom, evaluation comparison; Tag 0FNY, example-dual, finite free dual

proof.text: The degree-zero and degree-one maps are prescribed. Induction in the tensor recursion forces every positive map to equal the one in step 3. For $n>0$ the negative formula then forces the one in step 4. Equivalently, the evaluation identity determines the functional $p_{-n}(z)$ on every argument because $p_n$ is an isomorphism; equality on all local arguments is equality in the sheaf Hom of [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. This proves uniqueness of both families.

source.place: Tag 0GMX, evaluation-defined map; internal Hom definition in section-internal-hom

proof.text: We will use bases on localized sites. For $V\in\mathcal C$, the induced $u_V:\mathcal C/V\to\mathcal D/u(V)$ preserves finite limits and coverings: both are computed on underlying diagrams and covering families. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] to this functor. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] globally and on these slices, with the restrictions of $a$ and $b$. This identifies the tensor-formula module functors used here as the left adjoints in [lem-pur-ringed-site-pullback-localization-universes]; that theorem's slice continuity hypothesis follows from covering preservation. Its comparison identifies $F_{R,V}(P|_V)$ with $(F_RP)|_{u(V)}$ and identifies the slice unit with the restricted global unit; similarly for $S$. Thus a trivialization on $V$ pulls to one on $u(V)$, and its basis pulls to the unit image of that basis, because the localized coefficient unit is the multiplication map of step 1.

Choose a covering $\{V_i\to1_{\mathcal C}\}$ trivializing $P$ and write $e$ for its basis on one member. Put $v=c(e\otimes1)$, an $S$-basis of $Q$ there. The covering maps $u(V_i)\to1_{\mathcal D}$ cover by the assumptions on $u$. On each such member, let $\widehat e$ and $\widehat v$ denote the unit images in $F_R(P)$ and $F_S(Q)$, and put $e'=p(\widehat e)$ and $v'=q(\widehat v)$. These are bases by the unit-compatible localization comparison in step 6 and the coefficient units of step 1. The assumed degree-one square, with $\Theta_P$, says $v'=c'(e'\otimes1)$. Positive recursion sends $\widehat {e^{\otimes n}}$ to $(e')^{\otimes n}$ and likewise for $v$. For negative powers the basis assertion of [lem-pur-ringed-site-finite-free-dual-pullback] sends the pulled dual basis to the dual of the pulled basis; precomposition with $p_n^{-1}$ sends it to the dual basis of $(e')^{\otimes n}$, and likewise for $q_n$. Consequently $p_m,q_m$ send the corresponding signed bases to signed bases for every $m\in\mathbf Z$, including $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 0GMX and Tag 0FNY, pulled evaluation and dual bases; Tag 03EL, unit-normalized tensor comparison

proof.text: On these same charts, [lem-pur-signed-line-scalar-tensor-tower] gives $c_m(e^m\otimes1)=v^m$ and $c'_m((e')^m\otimes1)=(v')^m$ for every signed $m$. The common source of the proposed square, identified by $\Theta_{P^{[m]}}$, is a free rank-one $S'$-module sheaf with generator $g=\widehat {e^m\otimes1}$. The left composite takes $g$ first to $\widehat {v^m}$ and then to $(v')^m$. The right composite takes it to $(e')^m\otimes1$ and then to $(v')^m$. Both maps are $S'$-linear, so on every section $t g$ their value is $t(v')^m$; hence they coincide on each localized chart. The sheaf uniqueness axiom makes them equal globally. This proves the square simultaneously in positive, zero and negative degree, with arbitrary $a,b,\iota,\iota'$; each calculation used only balancing or evaluation.

tool_uses.why: Generic geometric inverse-image tensor structure on arbitrary small sites; the twist unit has no replacement for this site-theoretic tool.
Generic underived relative tensor comparison for arbitrary ringed topoi; used to construct tensor recursion and explicit scalar reassociation.
Generic evaluation-defined dual pullback isomorphism for finite locally free modules without flatness; used for negative powers, not a purity or six-functor route.
